item.title: Studio DRIFT makes the invisible force of wind visible in stunning new London installation
item.description: Amsterdam-based art studio DRIFT has unveiled Aeolus, a large-scale installation at London’s Ladbroke Hall that uses hundreds of glass rods and hidden lights to make the invisible movement of wind visible.

item.title: EU vies to expand role in Ukraine-Russia peace talks to influence US thinking
item.description: Brussels wants to turn the next round of trilateral peace talks betwen Ukraine, Russia and the US into a multilateral format with European representation.

item.title: Kenya: huge piles of rubble after high-rise building collapses
item.description: A multi-storey building under construction has collapsed in Nairobi, leaving a vast pile of rubble. Red Cross workers have arrived at the scene, where excavators are being used among the debris.

item.title: CICA members look to turn regional dialogue into action
item.description: The Conference on Interaction and Confidence-Building Measures in Asia (CICA) brought together member states to discuss regional security, economic cooperation and shared challenges, with a focus on strengthening the organisation's role and turning dialogue into practical action.

item.title: Melania Trump secures ceasefire in Russian-occupied Ukrainian city of Oleshky, White House says
item.description: The agreement, due to take effect on 29 October, is intended to allow humanitarian aid and civilian evacuations in a city where residents have endured years of Russian occupation, severe food shortages and dangerous attempts to escape.

item.title: Shamonda virus: First human case is ‘an alert’, not a reason to panic, says EU health agency
item.description: The first human case of Shamonda virus, confirmed in France, poses no wider threat to Europeans, the European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control (ECDC) told Euronews.

item.title: Wind-powered snow sleds and coral recovery hope: Positive environmental stories from 2026
item.description: Eco anxiety is very real, so we share this year's most uplifting stories to prove there’s hope for our climate.

item.title: Late invitations and spats leave Hungary’s 1956 commemoration with ‘modest’ guest list
item.description: Hungarian PM Péter Magyar had hoped to host top leaders in Budapest for the 70th anniversary of the 1956 revolution. But last-minute invitations and spats with Paris and Kyiv kept Macron, Tusk and Zelenskyy away, leaving only EU chiefs Ursula von der Leyen and António Costa attending.

item.title: Storm Austen batters France and UK with winds of up to 160 km/h
item.description: Huge waves, uprooted trees and damaged boats mark Storm Austen's arrival in France and the UK. Gusts of up to 160 km/h have battered Brittany, while fallen branches have blocked roads in southern England.

item.title: France's bond drama takes centre stage ahead of ECB rate decision
item.description: The European Central Bank is expected to hold rates next week as France's bond sell-off tightens borrowing conditions across the eurozone, while ECB President Christine Lagarde has made clear that the first steps to tackle French debt woes must come from Paris, not Frankfurt.

item.title: Ukraine hits Russian data centres in blow to Moscow's AI capabilities
item.description: Drones hit three Yandex facilities, a Sber centre and a VKontakte server farm across five Russian regions, causing persistent failures in payments, navigation and cloud services. Experts say restoring the infrastructure could take months or years.

item.title: A rhythmic gymnast’s journey from childhood dream to national pride
item.description: Azada reflects on her first international competition, representing Azerbaijan and her ambition to become a strong senior gymnast.

item.title: E9X: The battery-powered plane with 90 passengers on board and a range of 1,000 kilometres
item.description: Flying without kerosene is no longer just a dream, with pilots being trained to fly electric planes in the Netherlands. Before long, these battery-powered planes could be carrying 90 passengers and flying distances of up to 1,000 kilometres.

item.title: Belgium boosts heating-oil aid for vulnerable households as energy prices rise
item.description: Belgium is stepping up targeted aid to shield vulnerable households from soaring energy costs, but the limited support may fall short as prices rise.

item.title: France: shops barricaded in Lyon and Orléans for possible unrest as protests loom
item.description: Wooden boards are going up across France as shopkeepers brace for possible unrest. With a National Rally congress in Orléans and protests approaching in Lyon, businesses fear damage and disruption.

item.title: Trapped miner in coal mine in Turkey confirmed dead, bringing death toll to three
item.description: Three miners were killed and five injured, two of them seriously, in an explosion at a privately owned mine in northern Turkey.

item.title: Storm Austen hits northwestern France: 161,000 homes lose power
item.description: The first major autumn storm is sweeping across northwestern France. Named Austen by UK forecasters, it brings violent gusts, disrupts transport and causes power cuts.

item.title: World Culinary Awards: Which are the best airlines and airports for dining?
item.description: Where are the best places to eat in the skies or before you board? Airlines, airports and airport lounges were among the winners at this year’s World Culinary Awards.

item.title: First Russian diesel shipment is heading to US under Trump-Putin deal
item.description: The shipment, carrying about 40,000 tonnes of diesel, follows a deal that temporarily eased US sanctions on Russian diesel as Trump seeks to lower fuel prices.

item.title: From education to cancer care: Global summit calls for better support for children
item.description: Experts interviewed by Euronews explained why improving children's lives requires more than simply expanding access to essential services.

item.title: Suspect arrested after 1 killed and several injured in a shooting in Paris suburb
item.description: The man was arrested in nearby Coignieres after opening fire in Trappes and neighbouring La Verriere around 10:30 am, police said.

item.title: Gaza: Moment Israeli airstrike hits building in Nuseirat caught on camera
item.description: Footage captures the moment an Israeli strike hits a building in Gaza's Nuseirat camp. No deaths were reported, but images show a wounded person.

item.title: Starlink restrictions not lifted in Ukraine despite Trump's claims, defence officials say
item.description: Ukrainian forces continue to experience disruptions to critical battlefield communications despite Donald Trump's assertion that restrictions have been removed, raising fresh questions about Kyiv's dependence on an American-controlled satellite network.

item.title: Latest news bulletin | October 23rd, 2026 – Midday
item.description: Catch up with the most important stories from around Europe and beyond this October 23rd, 2026 - latest news, breaking news, World, Business, Entertainment, Politics, Culture, Travel.

item.title: France slips into contraction as Europe’s growth slows: How bad could it get?
item.description: France’s private sector contracted this month, dragging eurozone business activity growth to a four-month low amid political uncertainty and high energy costs.

item.title: Romania and EU accuse Russia of new drone attack as ship capsizes in Black Sea
item.description: A massive search and rescue operation is underway off the Romanian coast in the Black Sea following a new drone attack on a commercial ship that both the European Commission and Romania call as another Russian escalation.

item.title: French kids use AI far more than their parents think, survey finds
item.description: A new YouGov survey has found parents in France underestimate their children’s use of AI. While 40% of 11- to 12-year-olds report using general-purpose AI services like ChatGPT weekly, only 26% of parents realise their children are engaging with the technology.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV cancels Assisi trip on doctors' advice as he recovers from surgery
item.description: The pope's doctors said a follow-up chest X-ray confirmed he was recovering well. However, given the short time that has elapsed since the operation, they recommended as a precaution that he not make the trip to Assisi by helicopter.

item.title: Trump says he has the right to seek a third presidential term
item.description: US President Donald Trump has again suggested he could run for a third term in 2028, arguing that the 2020 election was stolen despite the US Constitution's two-term limit.

item.title: Oil spill hits UAE beaches as tanker attacks multiply near Hormuz
item.description: The UAE’s Ministry of Climate Change said teams were deployed to contain a spill affecting Umm Al Quwain’s beaches, days after a tanker was struck by a projectile off the UAE coast, causing a fire.

item.title: New 007 incoming: James Bond casting down to these actors according to insider reports
item.description: An official announcement regarding the new actor to portray James Bond is expected soon... And if reports are to be believed, one actor is emerging as the favourite to play the new 007.

item.title: Tributes paid to actor Tom Skerritt as star of Alien and Top Gun dies aged 93
item.description: Tom Skerritt, a Hollywood veteran actor, known for iconic roles in Alien and Top Gun, has died aged 93 of natural causes, according to a statement released by his family.

item.title: Fitch Ratings: Hungary could meet eurozone entry criteria by 2030
item.description: According to the credit rating agency, Hungary’s 2027 draft budget supports its aim of meeting the conditions for adopting the euro by the end of the decade.

item.title: Flash floods swamp southeast Australia as record October rainfall forces school closures
item.description: A television reporter abandoned his shoes and glasses and dived into rising floodwaters to save a driver whose car was sinking fast in Morayfield, Queensland.

item.title: Euronews Culture's Film of the Week: 'Clayface' – Gloopy, gruesome, but not quite great
item.description: An admirably dark and wince-inducing detour for DC Studios, who get a lot right with 'Clayface' when it comes to horror. However, the script lets it down in the second half, leading to a bold but uneven result.

item.title: Albania: Parliament descends into chaos as MPs clash over protests
item.description: Heated exchanges and chaotic scenes gripped Albania's parliament in Tirana on Thursday as rival MPs clashed inside, while student demonstrators continued their protests outside for a tenth day.

item.title: 'Music is medicine': RAYE wins Mercury Prize 2026 for her second album 'This Music May Contain Hope'
item.description: British jazz and soul artist RAYE beat competition from heavyweights including Paul McCartney, Florence + The Machine and favourite Olivia Dean. The Mercury Prize honours the best album released by a British or Irish artist each year.

item.title: Central Park’s horse-drawn carriages face ban as New York votes to end tourist attraction
item.description: Horse-drawn carriage rides could end in Central Park in June 2028, following years of debate over animal welfare and public safety.

item.title: Taiwan: Deadly Typhoon Champi brings travel chaos and school closures
item.description: Towering waves crashed against Taiwan's coastline as Typhoon Champi swept past the island on Friday, leaving one person dead, 94 injured and hundreds of flights cancelled.

item.title: Volvo Cars announces 2,500 job cuts as it swings to quarterly loss
item.description: Chinese ownership has not shielded Volvo Cars from competition in China, as the Geely-owned carmaker steps up its turnaround efforts amid pressure from local rivals, US tariffs and the removal of EV incentives.

item.title: Serbia election results expected to be ‘very tight’, analyst says
item.description: Berta López Domènech, an analyst at the European Policy Centre, said this is the first time an alternative to Serbia’s current leader, Aleksandar Vučić, has “real options” ahead of Sunday’s snap elections.

item.title: Less product, same price: what is supermarket ‘shrinkflation’?
item.description: From chocolate bars to toothpaste, everyday products are getting smaller while prices stay the same. Known as “shrinkflation,” this is making groceries increasingly expensive for Europeans, who end up paying the same for less.

item.title: Won a dream, got reality: why a German is selling his Haribo island
item.description: A private island, a log cabin and Canada on the doorstep: in 2005, Matthias R. from Bavaria won an unusual jackpot. Some 20 years on, he is looking for a buyer, as even wilderness needs upkeep - and it is a long way to go just for a short break.

item.title: A Budapest reset, and a scramble to get Ukraine peace talks back on track
item.description: Good morning. I’m Mared Gwyn. In this Friday edition: Ursula von der Leyen is set to become a headline act at Hungary’s 1956 revolution commemoration, and Europeans grapple with Trump’s “terrifying” Ukraine approach.

item.title: Could lab-made gold crash prices like diamonds? US start-up says it turned mercury into gold
item.description: Little-known San Francisco start-up Marathon Fusion says it has turned mercury into stable gold at ten times the rate of CERN's record, raising a question that has haunted the diamond trade: could lab-made gold one day sink the price of the mined metal?

item.title: Europe Today: France braces for fresh protests as EU leaders seek Hungary reset
item.description: France is bracing for another weekend of protests after last week’s demonstrations turned violent, as the government faces pressure to restore order. Meanwhile, EU leaders visit Hungary amid hopes of a reset in relations, while Serbia’s snap election puts President Aleksandar Vučić under pressure.

item.title: EU-Canada 'love story' needs more than warm words, senior MEP warns
item.description: European Parliament’s point man on Canada, Tobias Cremer, told Euronews that the planned “associate membership” should include an institutional framework formalising closer ties between the EU and Canada.

item.title: Lionel Messi sparks euphoria in Oviedo ahead of Princess of Asturias award ceremony
item.description: The Argentinian footballer has arrived in Spain's Oviedo region with his wife Antonela Roccuzzo, greeting hundreds of fans awaiting him. This Friday he will receive the 2026 Princess of Asturias Award for Sports.

item.title: Oil tops $114 as European shares fall and Kering tumbles
item.description: Rising energy prices added to inflation concerns as European shares fell and Kering tumbled on weak Gucci sales. An AI sell-off drove investors towards US bonds, while France’s borrowing costs remained above 5%.

item.title: Europe just had its deadliest summer. Which country was hit the hardest by extreme heat?
item.description: Europe faced its ‘worst summer on record’ for heat deaths – with climate change responsible for two-thirds.
